preconditions_if_revived: periodic provenance flush (instrumentation_flush_period_s > 0) so the edge-provenance JSONL is actually written
/Mapper/dump_pose_graph_now called at each boundary as an in-mapper barrier, with SHA-stamped files
scan-queue / accept-progress counters recorded before trusting the dump
old-topic and new synchronous snapshots stored in the same run
budget: place_A r2 S0/S1 first (2 runs), then at most place_B r1 L+/L- and place_C r1 L+/L- (4 runs), hard cap 8 including technical repairs
online_diagnostic.reason: the offline data already support stage attribution (accept-time identity for every keyframe, content times for every snapshot); the remaining questions are mechanism-level (why some runs form no effective closure) and would need the repaired observation chain rather than more of the old one

questions.q1_misattributed_action_gain: the entire late-published share: S1 0.08144 -> 0.00946; L- 0.11562 -> 0.04636; L+ 0.06485 -> 0.04360; per-run table in stage_attribution_correction.csv
questions.q2_recomputable_records: all 56 recorded stage gains recompute exactly; keyframe accept times and creation-stage attribution are recoverable; edge provenance enums and never-published edge sets are not (instrumentation gap, documented)
questions.q3_incremental_value_after_correction: yes but small and realisation-dependent: S0 zero, S1 ~0.009, L+ ~0.044 (5/12 exactly zero), L- ~0.046 (0/12 zero)
questions.q4_place_direction_difference: the mean direction difference disappears; a realisation asymmetry remains: L- created an effective closure in 12/12 main runs, L+ failed in 5/12 (A r2/r3 and all three B runs)
questions.q5_pre_action_explanation: no pre-action feature explains the remaining asymmetry; it clusters by place/run order (see DIRECTION_DIFFERENCE_EXPLANATION rows)
questions.q6_information_vs_gt: no measurable GT improvement: target error change ~+1e-4 m, robot SLAM error unchanged, relative pose error unchanged
questions.q7_localisation_error_needing_repair: no case-specific repair signal: robot SLAM error is centimetre-scale and does not accumulate through the action; target-state map error ~9.5 cm is constant across boundaries
questions.q8_best_fixed_action_sufficient: a fixed L- action is the most reliable default (0 zeros), but its expected increment (~0.046 nats) is far below the same-configuration re-execution scale (0.127 nats) per run, so single-run benefit is not demonstrable
questions.q9_method_necessity: no: no localisation value, no selection signal above realisation noise; the remaining interest is the closure-realisation mechanism itself

rationale: recorded stage gains are reproducible independently (all 56 runs), but the snapshot-difference attribution mixed stages: closures created during the return leg were published after the arrival boundary and landed in the action difference

after the FIXED_LINEARIZATION_FACTOR_DIAGNOSTIC attribution, the S1 action mean drops from 0.08144 to 0.00946 nats; L+ from 0.06485 to 0.04360; L- from 0.11562 to 0.04636; S0 stays exactly zero in 12/12
the recorded L+ minus L- direction difference (-0.05077 nats) collapses to -0.00277 (positive in 6/12 pairs) after the correction: the apparent direction effect was a publication-timing artifact

information gains never translated into localisation value: target-state map error change (final - before) is 0.000124 m mean, SLAM robot error change (tail - history) is 0.007033 m mean; no GT improvement accompanies the J_T gains

the mechanism is fully accounted for: every stage gain equals the marginal contribution of the closure edges added in that stage difference (0 law violations of 168 stage rows); zero-gain runs are runs whose action produced no effective closure
single_next_step: close the pure-rotation selection line and, if the revisit topic continues, restart it as a closure-realisation mechanism study using the repaired observation chain (periodic provenance flush + synchronous dump per boundary), beginning with a bounded place_B L+ zero-cluster replication (<=4 runs) instead of any further selector evaluation
